filename: Data-Driven Equation Discovery of a Cloud Cover Parameterization.pdf
title: Data-Driven Equation Discovery of a Cloud Cover Parameterization
venue: Journal of Advances in Modeling Earth Systems
code_availability: The cloud cover schemes and analysis code are preserved (Grundner, 2023) at http://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.7817391
testbed_rationale: High-resolution storm-resolving simulation data coarse-grained to standard climate model resolutions (80km, 40km, 20km) with public code and reproduction scripts, providing clear offline benchmarks for machine learning cloud parameterization and equation discovery.
pain_points: Neural networks act as black boxes, making post-hoc interpretation difficult and producing unreliable out-of-distribution predictions.
Symbolic regression genetic algorithms struggle to scale beyond 5-6 input features, necessitating sequential feature selection.
Large distribution shift between simulated cloud condensate (DYAMOND) and observational reanalysis (ERA5) causes direct zero-shot transfer failure without fine-tuning.
Storage and processing bottlenecks associated with several terabytes of high-resolution storm-resolving simulation outputs.
Shallow convection and stratocumulus clouds remain under-resolved even at kilometer-scale resolutions.
extraction_notes: The manuscript was accepted at JAMES in early 2024. While the parameterization targets the ICON Earth System Model, coupling was kept offline to evaluate inter-model and observational transferability independently of host model compensating biases.
